sections.markdown:
## C - Knowledge Dossier: Rules of the Road (Utah Handbook Sec 9, printed pp. 39-50)

Coverage basis: labelled pedagogic_emphasis; no official domain weights were verified on the selected pages.

FACT_ID: C-RR-01 | anchor: A39
A flex lane may show double-dashed yellow lines at its sides and overhead signals control use [A39].
A green arrow means the flex lane may be used; a red X means it must not be used [A39].
Some travel lanes carry one direction at certain times and the opposite direction at other times, so check usability before entering [A39].
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: C-RR-02 | anchor: A39
On a freeway maintain at least two seconds following distance behind the vehicle ahead, increased when conditions are adverse [A39].
Make no U-turns on a freeway and make no use of an entrance ramp to exit [A39].
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: C-RR-03 | anchor: A39
The emergency lane outside the solid white line is for emergency use only; passing there or stopping there to pick up passengers is not allowed [A39].
Generally travel near the speed of surrounding traffic but never above the posted limit, including when leaving the freeway [A39].
Pass only when safe [A39].
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: C-RR-04 | anchor: A39
A vehicle in the left lane approached from behind must move safely right so as not to impede traffic [A39].
Change freeway lanes only to pass, to exit, or to take the correct lane for a coming route separation [A39].
A citation for impeding may be issued when a driver stays in the left lane of a multi-lane highway while followed and does not let the follower pass [A39].
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: C-RR-05 | anchor: A40
Express lanes on I-15 are for high-occupancy use; vehicles with two or more persons may use them without charge [A40].
Motorcycles, buses, and vehicles bearing a registered clean-fuel C decal may also use the express lane without charge [A40].
Single-occupant drivers need an express pass through UDOT tied to an active account for charges based on rate and distance [A40].
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: C-RR-06 | anchor: A40
Crossing a double white line is not allowed [A40].
Move into or out of the carpool lane only at access points marked by white dotted striping rather than solid lines [A40].
Access points are about 3,000 feet long and found at nearly every interchange; exit the express lanes one interchange before the wanted exit is recommended [A40].
When followed by an emergency or police vehicle showing flashing lights, a right lane change out of the express lane is permitted when safe [A40].
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: C-RR-07 | anchor: A40
C decals let eligible single-occupant clean-fuel vehicles use express lanes without toll after a one-time 10 dollar registration fee [A40].
The decal is a small sticker inside the windshield to the right of the rear view mirror, and only certain clean-fuel vehicles qualify [A40].
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: C-RR-08 | anchor: A40
When entering a multi-lane highway use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, find a gap, merge, then cancel the signal [A40].
When exiting plan ahead, move to the exit lane early without a quick lane change, hold steady speed on the main road, then signal, enter the exit or deceleration lane, reduce to the posted exit speed, and cancel the signal [A40].
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: C-RR-09 | anchor: A41
Ramp meters on some Wasatch Front freeway on-ramps show alternating red and green lights and normally admit one vehicle per green unless posted differently [A41].
Metering applies only when many vehicles seek entry; a lighted meter-on sign at the on-ramp entrance shows when it is in effect, and when not lit entry is as usual [A41].
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: C-RR-10 | anchor: A41
A runaway vehicle ramp must not be used except in an emergency requiring it to stop the vehicle [A41].
Stopping, standing, or parking on or in the pathway of a runaway vehicle ramp is prohibited [A41].
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: C-RR-11 | anchor: A41
At a single-point urban interchange off-ramps and on-ramps sit diagonally adjacent above or below the freeway, with dash-line guidance and wrong-way signs on ramps [A41].
A U-turn from the off-ramp to re-enter the freeway is allowed when facing a green arrow at the start; complete the maneuver without stopping in the intersection even though a red arrow faces the on-ramp entry [A41].
A power outage there is not treated as a four-way stop; proceed with extreme caution and courtesy, with battery backup or officer control expected [A41].
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: C-RR-12 | anchor: A41
At every intersection slow down and search for controls, oncoming and cross traffic, pedestrians and bicyclists, road conditions, and view blockages [A41].
Do not assume others will obey signals or yield; be ready to avoid a crash [A41].
After stopping check traffic and bicyclists, look left, right, then left again before entering; when a light turns green confirm the path is clear of cross traffic [A41].
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: C-RR-13 | anchor: A42
Do not enter a lane only because an oncoming vehicle shows a turn signal; it may turn after passing or have left the signal on [A42].
Approaching an intersection check all directions, brake smoothly and evenly, and hold lane position [A42].
When stopping come to a complete stop behind signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, and when behind another vehicle leave room to see its rear tires [A42].
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: C-RR-14 | anchor: A42
When driving through an intersection check all directions, keep both hands on the wheel, slow down, yield to pedestrians and traffic in the intersection, and make no lane change inside it [A42].
After the intersection keep checking mirrors and traffic behind, accelerate smoothly, and when multiple lanes exist reach traffic speed, signal, check blind spots by head check and mirrors, then move to the right-most lane when safe if not already there [A42].
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: C-RR-15 | anchor: A42
At a continuous-flow left turn follow signs to the left side, obey the first signal and cross oncoming lanes on green, then obey the second far-left signal and turn left on green [A42].
Through travel at such an intersection is normal but a second light just past it may be red to let left-turners cross ahead [A42].
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: C-RR-16 | anchor: A42
At a continuous-flow right turn yield to traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians, then turn, merge, and continue [A42].
Free-right turns on red and traditional right-on-red are restricted there; obey posted controls for when right turns are permitted [A42].
A four-legged continuous-flow intersection applies displaced left turns on all four legs under the same rules [A42].
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: C-RR-17 | anchor: A43
In a diverging diamond interchange the non-freeway directions cross to the opposite side over or under the freeway, briefly driving on the opposite side, which removes many ramp left-turn conflicts [A43].
In a thru-U-turn layout left turns at the intersection are removed; drivers go through, make a signalized U-turn beyond it, return, then turn right [A43].
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: C-RR-18 | anchor: A43
Yellow markings divide opposing directions; white markings divide same-direction flow [A43].
A lane that separates an express or carpool lane from general lanes must not be crossed [A43].
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: C-RR-19 | anchor: A44
At a stop sign or signal stop behind the stop line or crosswalk; where no crosswalk is marked stop before the intersection or sign [A44].
Yield to pedestrians entering or in a crosswalk whether marked or not [A44].
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: C-RR-20 | anchor: A44
To use a shared center left-turn lane check mirrors and ahead, signal left, check the left blind spot, steer smoothly in, and turn when clear [A44].
Do not enter that lane more than 500 feet before the turn unless the last car is more than 500 feet from the intersection [A44].
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: C-RR-21 | anchor: A44
Utah basic speed law never permits more than is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions [A44].
Absent signs and special hazards the permitted speeds stated are 20 miles per hour at school buildings or grounds during recess and while children come or go during opening or closing hours or flashing lights operate; 25 miles per hour in any business or residential area; 55 miles per hour on major highways as posted; and 65, 70, 75, or 80 miles per hour on rural interstate highways, with transition zones marked by pavement markings and signs [A44].
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: C-RR-22 | anchor: A45
The law requires slowing at intersections and railroad crossings, around curves, at hilltops, on narrow or winding roads, near roadside pedestrians, heavy traffic, dangerous conditions, poor weather, unclear vision, highway work zones, near authorized vehicles flashing red, red and white, or red and blue lights, and whenever speed prevents staying in control or in one lane [A45].
Poor-weather illustrations include 10 miles per hour on ice or 25 miles per hour on a rainy-night highway possibly being too fast [A45].
Driving so slowly as to impede normal flow may draw a citation [A45].
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: C-RR-23 | anchor: A45
At a roundabout slow on approach, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, enter when clear, proceed through, and exit at the wanted street [A45].
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: C-RR-24 | anchor: A45
Traffic controls include signals, signs, markings, and directions from law enforcement, highway workers, and school crossing guards [A45].
Vertical signals show red, yellow, green from top to bottom; horizontal signals show red on the left, yellow in the middle, and green on the right; some sites use a single green, yellow, or red light [A45].
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: C-RR-25 | anchor: A45
A green light permits going through with caution if the way is clear; a green arrow permits only the arrow direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians still in the intersection [A45].
Yellow means the light is about to turn red; flashing yellow means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop [A45].
A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, since oncoming traffic holds green [A45].
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: C-RR-26 | anchor: A46
Red means stop before the intersection and wait behind the stop line, crosswalk, or intersection until green; right turn on red is allowed after a complete stop unless posted otherwise [A46].
Flashing red means stop and look both ways before entering [A46].
Right red arrow prohibits right turns and left red arrow prohibits left turns until an indication to proceed appears, except a stranded left-turner on a one-way street turning onto a one-way street may turn when safe if the arrow never changes [A46].
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: C-RR-27 | anchor: A46
Obey a police officer over traffic lights; stop when ordered even on green and turn when ordered even to go straight [A46].
Where signals are not working first come to a complete stop, then yield to any vehicle on the right unless a peace officer directs otherwise [A46].
A left-turner may face a green arrow for a protected turn, a solid green for a permitted turn, or a flashing yellow arrow for a permitted turn [A46].
Guide signs are square or rectangular in green, brown, or blue and point to roads, cities, towns, points of interest, hospitals, service stations, restaurants, and hotels [A46].
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: C-RR-28 | anchor: A47
A round yellow sign with X symbol and black RR warns to slow down, look, listen, and prepare to stop for a train or railroad vehicle [A47].
A white X-shaped Railroad Crossing sign warns a train or railroad vehicle is coming and requires stopping behind the stop line or before the intersection [A47].
Track-count signs may appear where more than one track exists, but not always, so always look for multiple tracks, trains, or railroad vehicles [A47].
When crossing look both ways, cross quickly without stopping on the tracks, wait until a passing train is well down the track, wait for raised gates and extinguished lights where present, and when stopping for traffic or a signal wait at the stop line before the tracks [A47].
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: C-RR-29 | anchor: A48
Warning signs are usually diamond shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols, covering lane ends, merging traffic, added lane, curves, divided highway begins or ends, intersections, side roads, T-intersections, no-passing zones, stop ahead, signals ahead, advisory speeds, school and pedestrian crossings, sharing with bicycles, bicycle crossings, and slippery-when-wet conditions [A48].
A yield sign requires slowing and yielding to traffic with the right-of-way [A48].
A left-only lane sign marks a lane only for left-turning vehicles, not for through travel or passing [A48].
One-way arrow signs allow travel only in the arrow direction; never drive the wrong way on a one-way street [A48].
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: C-RR-30 | anchor: A49
Work-zone signs are diamond or rectangular and orange with black letters or symbols, warning of workers, reduced speed, detours, slow machinery, or surface changes [A49].
Barriers bar entry to closed roads or danger areas; at a short-term signal stop at the white line if present [A49].
In work zones slow down, be ready to stop quickly, do not tailgate, obey flaggers, and fines for speeding there are doubled [A49].
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: C-RR-31 | anchor: A50
Never assume the right-of-way; judge safety in each case [A50].
Yield to a driver already in the intersection, to opposite-lane drivers when turning left, to the driver on the right when both reach a four-way stop together, to public-road drivers when entering from a driveway or private road, to interstate traffic when on the entrance ramp, and to pedestrians, bicyclists, and others still in the intersection [A50].
Courtesy is the key [A50].
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0060]

High-yield (ranked):
1) Signal meanings and turns on red and arrows [A45] [A46]; 2) Right-of-way at intersections, left turns, and four-way stops [A50]; 3) Speed limits by zone and required slow-down cases [A44] [A45]; 4) Left-lane impeding, lane-change limits, following distance, and freeway prohibitions [A39]; 5) Express-lane eligibility, double-white-line and access-point limits, and railroad-crossing stops [A40] [A47].

Misconceptions:
- Green light means unconditional go; handbook requires caution and a clear way, plus yielding on green arrows [A45].
- Right on red is always allowed; continuous-flow intersections restrict it and signs may prohibit it [A42] [A46].
- Left lane is for cruising; a follower behind requires moving right or risking an impeding citation [A39].
- Express lanes can be entered anywhere; crossing a double white line is illegal except at dotted access points [A40].
- Signals out means first-come-first-go only; rule requires a full stop then yield to the vehicle on the right [A46].
- Stopping on tracks to wait out traffic is acceptable; handbook forbids stopping on tracks and requires waiting at the stop line [A47].
- Work-zone speeding costs the normal fine; fines there are doubled [A49].

Mnemonics:
- Flex-lane read: Green-Go, Red-X-Rest [A39].
- Intersection scan: Left-Right-Left before entry [A41].
- Signal stack: Red-top to Green-bottom vertically, Red-left to Green-right horizontally [A45].

Glossary:
- Flex lane: rush-hour lane whose direction or use is set by overhead signals [A39].
- Express lane: I-15 high-occupancy lane usable free by qualifying vehicles or by pass holders [A40].
- Access point: dotted-line gap about 3,000 feet long for legal express-lane entry or exit [A40].
- Ramp meter: red-green on-ramp signal admitting normally one vehicle per green when meter-on is lit [A41].
- Runaway vehicle ramp: emergency-only stopping ramp, never for parking or standing [A41].
- Continuous flow intersection: layout displacing left turns to cross oncoming lanes before the main junction [A42].
- Shared center left-turn lane: middle lane for left turns only, entered within 500 feet of the turn [A44].
- Basic speed law: never exceed what is reasonable and prudent for conditions [A44].
- Protected versus permitted left: green arrow versus solid green or flashing yellow arrow [A46].
